title: Save manually before anything important
body:
You get **one save file per console user**: **one manual save** plus several autosaves. When you load, you resume exactly where you saved.

- Make a manual save before every boss and before any minigame or timed trade.
- There is no New Game+ and no post-game mode: finish what you still need (Skulltulas, Pieces of Heart, Great Fairies) **before** the final tower of Ganondorf's Castle.
- To keep a finished file, start the new run on another console user.

title: The Master Sword is your time machine
body:
In the Temple of Time, **draw the Master Sword from its pedestal** to jump seven years ahead and play as adult Link. **Put it back** to become a child again. You can go back and forth as often as you like.

- Some items are child-only and others adult-only: the inventory now splits them into child, adult and shared sections.
- Many secrets need both eras: plant a Magic Bean as a child and ride it as an adult, for example.
- Masks now work as an adult too.

title: Almost nothing is lost for good
body:
Since you can travel between eras, almost everything can be picked up later. This guide flags something as **missable** only when it has a window: night-only, one era only, or on a timer.

- The Business Scrub Piece of Heart near the castle costs 100 Rupees and **can only be bought as a child**: it is sold out as an adult.
- Several Biggoron Sword trade items expire within minutes: do not leave the chain half-done.
- Many Gold Skulltulas only come out at night: sleep in a bed or play the Sun's Song to change the time.
- When a tip relies on something the remake has not documented yet, we say so: "not yet confirmed for the remake".

title: Remake controls
body:
The layout changed from the original. By default:

- **X**: jump, anywhere (auto-jump is gone). It also climbs low ledges and gives a burst while swimming.
- **Hold A**: dash. A also talks, opens and picks up.
- **Y**: sword; hold and release for a spin attack.
- **ZL**: target (Options has two targeting modes).
- **ZR**: your only item button. **L/R** open a horizontal bar to swap it.
- **D-pad**: ← Ocarina, ↑ headgear (Lenses of Truth or masks), ↓ footwear (Iron or Hover Boots), → Navi.
- **Right stick**: free camera, Hyrule Castle Town included.

The jump attack is a two-step move, as in Breath of the Wild; Options lets you pick the original one-button version.

title: Navi, Fairy Thoughts and Gossip Stones
body:
**Navi only speaks when you call her** with → on the D-pad; during play she sometimes shows silent text bubbles.

- **Fairy Thoughts**: marks left by fairies all over Hyrule. Walk up and Navi reads them: advice and secrets. Play a song at one and it drops an item or restores your hearts.
- There are more Gossip Stones than before, and some tell new secrets.
- The 3DS version's **Sheikah Stones**, with their hint videos, are gone (per Zelda Wiki).

title: Threads of Time and the map
body:
**Threads of Time** is the new quest log: a tapestry that fills in as the story advances and tracks what you still have to do. Use it for long chains such as the Biggoron Sword trade.

- The new map **shows which collectibles you are missing in each area**, and the mini-map is in full colour.
- There are no new warp points: you travel with the warp songs, Epona and Farore's Wind.

title: Rupees and wallets
body:
Shops cost more than in the original, but wallets hold twice as much:

- You start with room for **200 Rupees**.
- **Adult's Wallet** (10 Gold Skulltulas): **500**.
- **Giant's Wallet** (30 Gold Skulltulas): **1,000**.

You will spend on Great Fairy offerings, on the Business Scrub's 100-Rupee Piece of Heart and in shops. The **Gold Rupee** is worth 200: you get it for all 10 Big Poes and for 100 tokens at the House of Skulltula. When your wallet is full, extra Rupees are lost.

title: The five bottles
body:
There are now **5 bottles** (one more than the original). Get them early: they hold fairies, potions, milk, bugs for soft soil and Big Poes.

- **New**: lend a hand at the Potion Shop in Hyrule Castle Town.
- The **Poe Collector** gives you a bottle for **5 Big Poes** (was 10). Hyrule Field's Big Poes are marked by purple lanterns.
- The others are presumably where they were, not yet confirmed for the remake: the Cucco Lady in Kakariko (7 Cuccos), Talon's Cucco game at Lon Lon Ranch and Ruto's Letter.

A fairy in a bottle revives you when you run out of hearts: carry at least one into every boss.

title: Magic
body:
Magic comes from the Great Fairies and is spent on spells and the Lenses of Truth.

- **Lenses of Truth**: drain magic **while you wear them**; take them off as soon as you have seen what you were looking for.
- **Farore's Wind**: now costs **2 magic** (was 6) and returns you to the exact spot you marked. The point can only be replaced, not dispelled.
- **Din's Fire**: plays out in real time, without a pause.
- The improved spin attack no longer uses magic.

Top up with Magic Jars and green potions before a dungeon full of invisible walls.

title: Great Fairies ask for Rupees
body:
The **6 Great Fairies** are still there, but each now asks for a **Rupee offering** that grows with every fountain (one review says up to 500). Upgrade your wallet before going for the last ones.

- Their gifts show up on the **Collection** screen: Gift of Improved Spin, Gift of Doubled Magic and Gift of Halved Damage.
- Zelda Wiki says two fountains swapped: **Din's Fire** would be on Death Mountain and the improved spin attack near Hyrule Castle. Other guides still give the original layout: check it in your game.
- The exact offering amounts are not documented yet.

title: Get the Echo Gem early
body:
At **20 Gold Skulltulas**, the House of Skulltula in Kakariko Village gives you the **Echo Gem**, which replaces the Stone of Agony. **Equip it**: it blinks on screen and vibrates when a Gold Skulltula is nearby, even where one only appears at night.

- Hidden grottos no longer need a detector: they show up as cracked ground or rocks.
- Ten Skulltulas live in soft soil: release bugs from a bottle to dig them out.
- Start hunting in Kokiri Forest: the first 10 get you the Adult's Wallet.

title: Day, night and beds
body:
The day/night cycle is **longer** than in the original, and time also passes in settlements. NPCs follow schedules and many go to bed at night.

- **Sleep in a bed or a bedroll** to change the time.
- The **Sun's Song** still skips to day or night instantly.
- Many Gold Skulltulas only come out at night, and as an adult Stalchildren also appear at night in Hyrule Field.

title: Hearts: 36 pieces and 8 containers
body:
You start with 3 hearts. There are **36 Pieces of Heart** (every 4 make one) and **8 Heart Containers**, one per boss: **20 hearts** in total.

- Pieces and containers are **no longer picked up by touching them**: press **A**. Fairies work the same way.
- Three pieces moved: the Ice Cavern one is gone (a Business Scrub in Death Mountain Crater sells it now), the Hyrule Field lone-tree grotto piece is now a chest you open with time travel, and the Hyrule Field Business Scrub piece costs 100 Rupees and needs a password.

title: Combat basics
body:
Lock on with **ZL** and fight face to face: while targeting you circle the enemy and dodge with more control. What is new in the remake:

- You can now **jump** with X mid-fight and move while aiming.
- Iron Knuckle axe swings **can be blocked with your shield**.
- The **Mirror Shield** reflects Beamos lasers.
- ReDeads charge at you up close; Wallmasters cast a purple glow before they drop.
- **Deku Nuts** stun almost everything near you, and **Bombchus** run along walls to far-off switches.

There is no difficulty selector: many reviewers found it easier than the original.

title: Time travel
body:
The adventure has two eras: **child Link** (Kokiri Forest, the three Spiritual Stones) and **adult Link**, seven years later (the five temples). You switch in the Temple of Time with the Master Sword.

- Drawing the sword the first time opens a path to the Sacred Realm and Ganondorf walks in behind you: a new remake cutscene.
- Plant Magic Beans in soft soil as a child to ride up to high places as an adult.
- Some chests depend on both eras: the Hyrule Field Piece of Heart chest is sealed as a child and empty as an adult, and a Fairy Thought holds the solution.
- After your first visit as an adult, go back to Kakariko Village as a child and talk to Kaepora Gaebora to open the Hall of Fallen Foes.

title: Songs: buttons and microphone
body:
It is the same **12 songs plus the Scarecrow's Song**, with the same teachers and destinations. Take out the Ocarina with ← and play them three ways:

- With the **A, X, Y, L and R** buttons.
- By **humming** or playing a real instrument into the Switch 2 microphone.
- Hold **ZL** for the list of learned songs. The cutscenes after a song can be skipped.

Notes from the games.gg guide (one source, but all 12 line up):

- **Zelda's Lullaby**: Y X A Y X A
- **Saria's Song**: R A Y R A Y
- **Epona's Song**: X Y A X Y A
- **Sun's Song**: A R X A R X
- **Song of Time**: A L R A L R
- **Song of Storms**: L R X L R X
- **Minuet of the Forest**: L X Y A Y A
- **Bolero of Fire**: R L R L A R A R
- **Serenade of Water**: L R A A Y
- **Nocturne of Shadow**: Y A A L Y A R
- **Requiem of Spirit**: L R L A R L
- **Prelude of Light**: X A X A Y X
- **Scarecrow's Song**: 8 notes of your choice (for Bonooru as a child, Pierre as an adult).

title: Masks, as an adult too
body:
The Happy Mask Shop in Hyrule Castle Town still lends masks for you to sell. What is new:

- Masks can be worn **as an adult**. They go in the headgear slot: assign them to ↑ on the D-pad from the Equipment menu.
- The **Mask of Truth** now also lets you **hear what characters think**, on top of talking to Gossip Stones.
- The Young Link and Young Zelda amiibo give masks styled after the Nintendo 64 models.

The shop's rotation and the Mask of Truth requirements are not documented for the remake yet.

title: Lenses of Truth
body:
The Lens of Truth is now the **Lenses of Truth**: goggles you **wear on your head** (↑ on the D-pad, the same slot as masks). You get them in the Bottom of the Well.

- While you wear them, a purple eye on screen reveals fake walls, invisible floors and hidden enemies.
- They drain magic **the whole time you wear them**: take them off with ↑ when you do not need them.
- They are key in the Bottom of the Well, the Shadow Temple, the Mirage Desert and the Gerudo Proving Grounds.

title: Boots on the D-pad
body:
The **Iron Boots** and **Hover Boots** are your footwear: they sit on ↓ on the D-pad and go on and off **instantly**, without opening the menu. Choose which pair ↓ uses from the Equipment menu.

In the Water Temple this changes everything: sinking and floating back up no longer means pausing. The water levels there work as before (three heights you set with Zelda's Lullaby at the Triforce marks), and some walls are now lattices you can see the next room through.

title: Aiming: buttons or motion
body:
The Fairy Slingshot, Fairy Bow, Hookshot and Boomerang aim **in third person**, and you can move while aiming.

- In Options you choose stick aiming or **motion controls** (gyro), and you can invert the axes.
- The game can be finished without motion or touch controls.

title: HUD: Standard, Pro and Master
body:
Options offers three screen presets:

- **Standard**: all the information.
- **Pro**: the bare minimum.
- **Master**: nothing on screen, not even the lock-on marker or the reticle.

It is the closest thing to a hard mode: the remake has no difficulty selector.

title: Heat and lava
body: In Death Mountain Crater and the Fire Temple **there is no heat countdown any more**: without the Goron Tunic you lose hearts fast right away. And **lava kills on contact**. Put on the Goron Tunic before you go in.

title: Less rushing: almost every timer is gone
body:
The remake removes most puzzle countdowns, the heat timer and the final castle escape timer. In the Forest Temple, for example, the sliding-block puzzle has no time limit any more, although you need the right pieces.

The Biggoron trade items and some minigames still run on a clock.

title: What changed from the original?
body: **The adventure is the same: same dungeons, same order, same bosses.** What changed: the controls (jump on X, boots and Lenses on the D-pad), the free camera, several maps merged with no loading screens, some puzzles (above all in the Forest and Water Temples), some place and item names, plus new features such as the Hall of Fallen Foes, Fairy Thoughts, Threads of Time, a fifth bottle and the Echo Gem.

title: Does it include Master Quest?
body: **No.** The remake shipped without Master Quest. Dataminers found incomplete Master Quest data that would unlock through DLC, but Nintendo has announced nothing.

title: Is there a hard mode or Hero Mode?
body: **There is no difficulty selector and no Hero Mode.** The closest thing is the Pro and Master HUD presets, which hide the on-screen information.

title: Is there New Game+ or a post-game?
body: **There is no New Game+.** Finish your collectibles before the final tower and make a manual save before the last boss.

title: How many save files can I have?
body: **One per console user**, with one manual save and several autosaves. You cannot rename Link, and loading puts you where you saved, not at your house or the Temple of Time.

title: How do I jump?
body: **With X, any time.** The automatic jump at ledges is gone. X also climbs low ledges and gives you a burst while swimming; child Link jumps shorter than adult Link.

title: Why do I only have one item button?
body: **The remake uses ZR alone for items.** Press L or R to open a horizontal bar and swap quickly. The Ocarina, headgear, footwear and Navi each have a fixed D-pad button.

title: How do I put on the Iron Boots?
body: **With ↓ on the D-pad.** Boots are footwear and go on and off instantly. Pick in the Equipment menu whether ↓ uses the Iron or the Hover Boots.

title: How do I use the Lenses of Truth?
body: **Put them on with ↑ on the D-pad.** They are goggles: they reveal what is hidden while you wear them and drain magic the whole time.

title: Where is the Stone of Agony?
body: **It is gone: the Echo Gem replaces it**, and the House of Skulltula gives it to you at 20 tokens. The Echo Gem detects Gold Skulltulas; hidden grottos are now visible as cracked ground.

title: Are the Gold Skulltulas in the same places?
body: **Most are, but some moved and nobody has published which yet.** There are still 100 (56 outdoors and 44 in dungeons) and the per-area split is the same, except Hyrule Field (3, was 2) and Lon Lon Ranch (3, was 4). Our list starts from the 3DS positions and flags the areas whose layout changed. Equip the Echo Gem to find the ones you are missing.

title: How many Pieces of Heart are there?
body: **36 pieces and 8 containers**, as always: 20 hearts with the starting 3. Remember they are now picked up by pressing A.

title: What happened to the Ice Cavern Piece of Heart?
body: **It is not there any more.** A Business Scrub in Death Mountain Crater now sells it for 100 Rupees; buy it as a child.

title: What is the Business Scrub password?
body: **A new side quest tied to a Hyrule Field Piece of Heart.** The Business Scrub in a grotto near Hyrule Castle, north-east of Hyrule Castle Town, sells the piece for 100 Rupees only if you give it the password, and it is sold out as an adult. Where you get the password is not well documented yet.

title: How many bottles are there?
body: **Five.** The new one comes from the Potion Shop in Hyrule Castle Town once you help the shopkeeper.

title: How many Big Poes do I need?
body: **5 for the bottle and all 10 for a Gold Rupee.** Bring them to the Poe Collector. Hyrule Field's Big Poes are marked by purple lanterns.

title: How many Rupees can I carry?
body: **200 at the start, 500 with the Adult's Wallet and 1,000 with the Giant's Wallet.** Both wallets come from the House of Skulltula (10 and 30 tokens).

title: Why does the Great Fairy want Rupees?
body: **In the remake every Great Fairy asks for a Rupee offering, and it grows with each fountain.** Save up and upgrade your wallet before you visit them.

title: Where do I get Din's Fire?
body: **Not confirmed yet.** Zelda Wiki says the remake puts it at the Great Fairy fountain on Death Mountain, swapped with the improved spin attack, which moves to Hyrule Castle. Other guides still place it at Hyrule Castle, as in the original.

title: Which buttons play the songs?
body: **A, X, Y, L and R, or hum into the Switch 2 microphone.** The Mechanics section lists the notes for all 13 songs. Hold ZL with the Ocarina out to see the ones you have learned.

title: Can I wear masks as an adult?
body: **Yes.** In the remake masks work in both eras; they go in the headgear slot (↑).

title: How do I unlock the Hall of Fallen Foes?
body: **After you first reach the adult era, return to Kakariko Village as a child and meet Kaepora Gaebora.** From then on you enter in either era by resting in a bed or bedroll. It replaces the 3DS Boss Challenge.

title: Where are the Sheikah Stones?
body: **They are not in the remake** (per Zelda Wiki). Hints now come from Navi, Fairy Thoughts and Gossip Stones.

title: How do I switch between day and night?
body: **Sleep in a bed or a bedroll, or play the Sun's Song.** The natural cycle is longer than in the original.

title: Can I turn off the HUD?
body: **Yes: the Master preset shows nothing**, not even the reticle or the lock-on marker. Pro keeps the bare minimum.

title: Is the heat timer still there without the Goron Tunic?
body: **There is no timer, but it is worse:** without the Goron Tunic you lose hearts fast as soon as you enter, and lava kills on contact.

title: Is there a countdown in the castle escape?
body: **No.** The final escape was reworked: Zelda holds back a horde and freezes the ReDeads, there is a gap you cross with the Hookshot, and no countdown.

title: What do amiibo give?
body: **Nothing essential.** Young Link and Young Zelda give retro masks; other Zelda amiibo give random consumables. Turn amiibo on in the game's settings first.

title: Is there fast travel?
body: **Only the usual kind.** Nintendo tried new warp points and removed them to keep the pacing: use Sheik's warp songs, Farore's Wind (now 2 magic) and Epona.

title: Is there Latin-American Spanish?
body: **Yes: Latin-American Spanish text and voices**, plus a Castilian Spanish dub. Voices are in the cutscenes; Link only grunts. The Spanish side of this guide uses the official Latin-American names where known and adds the English name in brackets otherwise.

title: Hall of Fallen Foes
body:
A dream-world gallery with **statues of every enemy you have defeated**. Each statue gives some lore, where the enemy lives and what helps against it. It replaces the 3DS version's Boss Challenge.

- **Getting in**: after first reaching the adult era, go back to Kakariko Village as a child and talk to Kaepora Gaebora. Afterwards, rest in any bed, bedroll or glowing green carpet.
- **Rematches**: touch a boss or mini-boss statue to fight it again; your time is recorded.
- **Boss gauntlets**: limited hearts and items. They pay Rupees you spend on upgrades inside the hall.
- Clear a gauntlet and Kaepora leaves a trophy at your house in Kokiri Forest.
- It is a dream: dying or using up items there has no consequences.

title: Master Quest: not included
body: **The remake does not include Master Quest.** Dataminers MrCheeze and OatmealDome found "MQ" strings and incomplete Master Quest data (a mirrored world, changed dungeons) that would unlock **by owning DLC**. Eiji Aonuma said Nintendo wants to "leave future possibilities open", but nothing has been announced. Until then, treat it as a rumour.

title: No Hero Mode or New Game+
body: There is no hard mode, Hero Mode or New Game+, and no difficulty selector. For a challenge, use the **Master** HUD preset (nothing on screen) and the Hall of Fallen Foes boss gauntlets.

title: ZELDA NOTES
body:
The **ZELDA NOTES** app (inside the Nintendo Switch App on your phone) adds to the game:

- A live map, Today's Record and play statistics.
- **Gossip Quests**: find in-game places from photos and earn points you trade for ocarina sheet music.
- The Threads of Time tapestry, the Hall of Fallen Foes, a photo studio, an ocarina player and a daily quiz.

None of it is needed to complete the game.

title: House of Skulltula rewards
body:
Hand Gold Skulltula tokens to the cursed family in Kakariko Village:

- **10**: Adult's Wallet (up to 500 Rupees).
- **20**: **Echo Gem**, the Skulltula detector (replaces the Stone of Agony).
- **30**: Giant's Wallet (up to 1,000 Rupees).
- **40**: 20 Bombchus.
- **50**: a Piece of Heart.
- **100**: a **Gold Rupee** (200 Rupees), and you can come back for another any time.

title: Poe Collector
body:
Catch Big Poes on horseback in Hyrule Field (look by the purple lanterns), bottle them and sell them to the Poe Collector:

- At **5 Big Poes**: a bottle (it used to take 10).
- At **all 10**: a **Gold Rupee**.

title: amiibo and retro masks
body:
Turn amiibo on in the game's settings before you scan them.

- **Young Link** and **Young Zelda** (new amiibo, out in 2027): unlock **retro masks** styled after the Nintendo 64 models.
- **Other Zelda amiibo**: random consumables such as bombs, Magic Jars, Deku Sticks and Nuts or Business Scrub Seeds.

None of them gives anything essential.

title: Play a song to a Fairy Thought
body: Once Navi has read a Fairy Thought, take out the Ocarina and play any song: it drops an item or restores your hearts. A quick way to heal far from a shop.

title: Business Scrub Seeds
body: A new remake item. Use a **Business Scrub Seed** and a wandering Business Scrub shows up with its shop wherever you are. They are in new chests around Hyrule and also come from some amiibo. Where each chest is has not been documented yet.

title: Grottos in plain sight
body: Hidden grottos are no longer invisible: look for **cracked ground or rocks** and open them with a bomb or the Megaton Hammer. One guide says the Song of Storms reveals even more hidden holes (not yet confirmed).

title: The Mask of Truth reads minds
body: Wear it and talk to people: besides understanding Gossip Stones, you now **hear what characters are thinking**, with a purple effect on the text box.

title: Details you notice on a replay
body:
- The castle courtyard window that used to show Mario portraits now shows the Threads of Time tapestry.
- Both ocarinas hang from Link's belt, and his fingers move with every note.
- Navi has a different dance for each song.
- Zora Domain thaws after you beat Morpha.
- Kill all of Dead Hand's hands in the Bottom of the Well and it is forced to surface.
- Jo, one of the Poe sisters in the Forest Temple, is now deep red.
